Amy Jackson Mora Wash May 10th, 1920. C.V. Peel Special Agent in Charge Agricultural Trade School Tacoma Washington Dear Sir: I am sending $15.00 (fifteen dollars) for transportation for Miss Amy Jackson. I am little late in sending the money as I was away from home. Very truly yours, Mr. Mark Williams P.S. Miss Amy Jackson has completed her terms of enrollment and would like to see her come home. (Thank You) FOR FILE DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Quileute Day School, MORA, WASH. June 20, 1919. Mrs. E. S. Hammond, Sup't Customan Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Dear Sir: It is found advisable to place this money to the credit of Amy Jackson, and not more than fifty cents should be drawn out by her at one time. If she deserts from the school she could not reach Seattle with fifty cents and continue her journey. I have already had some inquiries as to whether she was coming home for vacation or not. The parties are the ones wanting her hand in marriage. I would rather have her away another year as she is a pest and will be constantly in mischief. Please consider this confidential. Yours truly, A.T. Markishtain N.B. In case of sickness, if quite serious, ask parents to come after her and have them promise to return her before school opens and to discipline her at home. Have had reports of her being in the hospital. W.S. M Dear Avery, I am sending you $18.37 (thirteen dollars) for your return fare. We are going to have a Fourth of July here just collect the money this morning and made $13.75. We are all well. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., June 16, 1919 Teacher In Charge Noah Bay Indian Agency Mora, Wash. Dear Sir: I am returning herewith the letter and Money Order for Amy Jackson as per your telegram. Very respectfully, Superintendent. /MC Enc. Cushman Indiana School Tacoma, Washington April 5, 1919. Mrs. Mark Williams Forks, Washington. Dear Friend: Amy Jackson is well. She had a spell of sickness but has fully recovered. I will tell her that you have not heard from her and will have her write you. Very truly yours, Superintendent Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Washington April 5, 1919. Mrs. Nicholson Matron, Cushman School. Dear Mrs. Nicholson: I am in receipt of a letter from Mrs. Mark Williams, saying thru Mr. Markishtum, that she has not heard from her daughter, Amy Jackson for over two months. Of course she was in quarantine up to the 14th of March, but she has had plenty of time since then to write to her parents. Please have her do so at once. A letter will reach her parents at Forks, Washington. Respectfully, Superintendent 5-1142 DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Mora, Wash., March 27, 1919. Mr. E. W. Hammond, Supt. Cushman School, Tacoma, Wash. Dear Sir: Mrs. Mark Williams, mother of Amy Jackson, came to my office a day or two ago and wanted me to ask you if Amy was well. She has not written to them for over two months and they were anxious to know about her. Mr. Mark Williams stated that a letter would reach him at Forks, Washington. Yours truly, H. T. Markishium, Teacher in Charge Amy, you must write your mother at once. Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Jan. 31, 1919. Mr. H. T. Markishtum, Mora, Washington. My Dear Mr. Markishtum: Your letter of January 18th is hereby acknowledged. Amy Jackson arrived at the school safely and appears to be enjoying herself except for an attack of chicken pox. She is contented at school, and if her relatives will leave her in peace, she will remain so. Very sincerely yours, Superintendent EHH-S DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Mora, Wash., Jan. 18, 1919. Mr. E. H. Hammond, Supt. Cushman Trade School, Tacoma, Wash. Dear Sir: Herewith are enclosed letters for Amy Jackson. They were placed in my care at the postoffice by the postmistress at Mora. I would advise that these letters be opened by yourself or the matron in charge at her quarters, as the character of the letters can then be determined, whether the letters are for pure friendship, that they may be for a higher ideal or worthy of delivery to her. Amy is inclined to be weak morally and by strict discipline her morals may be changed, with surroundings foreign from an Indian village, such as found in a boarding or training school. Her guardians (step-father and a deaf mother) lack control and discipline over her. Her home surroundings are not elevating. She escapes at her will from home into questionable company. It is my advice that she be kept in school during vacation. She roamed here and there last summer without any escort or chaperone, giving Doctor Woods, (superintendent), myself and our police much trouble and annoyance. At different times during her stay here and at Neah Bay for her vacation from Cushman, young men approached us for consent to marry her and being too young they were advised not to annoy as she was not of age yet. I hope that you will not take this as an intrusion upon Amy's character, on your time or affairs. Yours truly, H.T. Markeshtum, Teacher Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Nov. 15, 1918. Mr. Henry T. Markishtum, Lapush, Washington. Dear Mr. Markishtum: I enclose herewith a check for $4.30, balance to the credit of Amy Jackson. On leaving for vacation last summer, Amy Jackson after paying her fare home could deposit only this amount and she promised faithfully to return last September. I gave her leave of absence believing that she would keep her word. Please see her parents and have them give her sufficient money to pay her way back. Clear Waters Wash. 12-15-18. Dear Amy, I'm going fine in here. I'm enjoying myself every way. I haven't got a letter from you ever since I got over here. What is the matter, are you dead or alive yet, tell me. How is the people over there, I heard some of them died, tell me who died so I will know. People over at hoguian are just dying by sickness. Doctors don't know what kind of sickness it is. Just took sick overnight and died. The hospital is just full, and too great big hall. And we are going to have a big time over here. Bill Sam he is going to kill one more more haha. I wish you was here. We are going to have it tomorrow. And we are going to celebrate Christmas to have a good time. What are you going to do Christmas. I will send you an postal card and that's all I'm going to say. So goodbye I'm going to cut wood. Ha Ha. Yours truly, Coist Morganworth Clear Waters P.O. Miss Amy Jackson Mora Nash 1918 Dear Amy Please let me know all the news up there and hope you won't get sick I understand nearly everybody is sick here Oed LaPresh William fine and dandy. So good Bye From a Friend HH Salto Mrs HAPPINESS is a perfume you cannot pour on others, without getting a few drops yourself. We, the undersigned, respectfully request that leave of absence be granted ............................................... .................................................................................................................... from June 15, 1918 to Sept. 5, 1918 to enable them to visit her home. We hereby agree to pay all expenses, including round-trip railroad fares, sleeping-car fares, meals, lodging, stage fares, telegraph and telephone messages, and other incidental expenses connected with the visit. We further agree that said pupil shall be returned to the Cushunum school on or before the last day of the leave of absence. We further agree to deposit with the superintendent of the school sufficient money to defray all expenses to be incurred, and should the pupils, or any one of them, fail to return to school at such time as may be agreed upon by the parents or guardian and the superintendent of the school in which the pupils are enrolled, the amount of money remaining with the superintendent, necessary to the return transportation of the pupil or pupils so neglecting to return, shall be forfeited to the Government; provided, however, that in all cases where it can be shown that there were justifiable reasons for the failure of the return of the pupil the forfeiture of the funds shall not take place. If the pupil neglecting to return is from a reservation, the superintendent of the reservation shall certify to the reasons for the nonreturn of the pupil or pupils. If a pupil's home is not on a reservation, then the certificate of some reputable, disinterested citizen of the community may be requested as to the reasons for the nonreturn of the pupil or pupils. ............................................................ This form must be executed in duplicate when a child is transferred from a reservation to a nonreservation school. The Superintendent of the nonreservation school will retain the original for his files, and the duplicate shall be deposited in the reservation school records. The reservation superintendent should send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate as provided by law. All the blank spaces in the present form must be filled in. If the information called for on any part of the blank is not known, that fact should be stated. No space should be left unfiled. Whenever the parents are living or dead, their names must be given. The person who signs the blank as consenting to the transfer should indicate his relation to the applicant by marking out the word "parent," "guardian," or "next of kin," leaving unmarked only the title appropriate to the signer. The enrollment of Indian pupils in nonreservation schools is governed by the "Rules for the Indian Service, 1913," sections 12, 13, 14, 15, 18, 19, 36, 112, 113, 114, 117, 118, 124 (b). The Rules should be consulted before filling out the application blanks. RECORD CARD—PREVOCATIONAL DIVISION. Each girl should devote 40 weeks to the work of this department during the three prevocational years. When she has accomplished the work as outlined in the course of study in a satisfactory manner, a suitable rating should be recorded. Ratings must be based on a practical application as well as a knowledge of the principles involved. Ratings should be excellent (E), good (G), fair (F). If pupil's work is not worthy of a rating of fair, no grade should be recorded. Under "Remarks" mention anything that indicates interest, conduct, and proficiency of the pupil. This card should be filed in folder for record of pupil (5-197).
